data.name: Ajeet
data.long_meaning: The name Ajeet is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘aj’ meaning ‘not’ and ‘it’ meaning ‘death’. It signifies someone who is invincible and cannot be defeated by death or adversity. In Hindu mythology, Ajeet is the name of a warrior god, who is described as the unconquerable and the invincible.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ajeet is deeply rooted in Indian culture, particularly in Sikhs and some Hindu communities. It is believed that bearing this name brings blessings of strength, courage, and victory. Historically, it was given to warriors and soldiers to inspire fearlessness in battle. In the modern world, naming a child Ajeet is a way to instill a sense of determination and unconquerable spirit from an early age.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism and Sikhism, Ajeet represents the universal truth that death is an inevitable part of life but does not have the power to defeat an individual's spirit or soul. The name is a reminder of the impermanence of worldly desires and the need to focus on the eternal. It evokes a sense of inner strength and resilience in the face of challenges, inspiring a deep spiritual connectivity to the ultimate truth of life and death.

historical_references.reference: Ajeet was a legendary king of the Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar, who ruled during the 11th and 12th centuries. He is said to have defeated the invading Ghaznavid army led by Muhammad Ghori in the Battle of Chandawar in 1192 CE.
historical_references.context: Battle of Chandawar against Muhammad Ghori's Ghaznavid army

historical_references.reference: Ajeet is also known as Ajay Singh and is believed to have ruled Mewar from 1142 CE to 1178 CE, and is considered one of the greatest rulers in the history of the Rajput kingdom. During his reign, he expanded his territory and established a strong military force, which helped him to resist external invasions.
historical_references.context: Expansion of Mewar territory and establishment of a strong military force
